operation.description: Reduce one bounded polynomial modulo a bounded ideal in QQ[x_1, x_2, ..., x_n] using a Groebner basis remainder. Returns the exact remainder and whether the polynomial is in the ideal; a computation that exceeds the enforced wall-time bound returns a typed TIMEOUT outcome instead of a remainder.

examples.description: Reduce x^2 modulo <x^2 - y^2> in Q[x,y]; the remainder is y^2, so x^2 is not in the ideal.
examples.name: normal_form_xy

CanonicalRational.description: A reduced rational whose denominator is positive and whose zero is 0/1.

den.description: Positive canonical decimal denominator; together with num it must be reduced, and integers use den='1'.
den.title: Den

num.description: Canonical decimal numerator of the reduced rational.
num.title: Num

RationalPolynomialIdeal.description:
A finitely generated ideal in one explicitly ordered ``QQ`` ring.

Generator lists are presentations, not canonical bases.  Every generator
nevertheless carries the same authoritative ring so ideals can pass
directly between operations without rendering or reparsing expressions.
RationalPolynomialIdeal.title: RationalPolynomialIdeal

terms.description: Nonzero monomials in descending lexicographic order of their exponent tuples (highest first). For one variable, list [2] before [0].
terms.title: Terms

input_schema.description:
Reduce one polynomial modulo an ideal's Gröbner basis.

``monomial_order`` names the order of the Groebner basis the reduction
uses; normal forms depend on it, so it is part of the public contract.
input_schema.title: IdealNormalFormRequest
